subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: Should OpenClaw core own a temp artifact provenance and cleanup model, and if so which parts are core guardrails versus plugin/ClawHub workflow policy?
rationale: The safety goal fits VISION.md priorities, but implementing it crosses storage policy, cleanup authority, agent/tool APIs, doctor/runtime guardrails, and core-vs-plugin boundaries that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Core guardrails plus plugin seam
options.body: Core would cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance seam, while workflow-specific classifications such as audit/review staging stay in plugins or ClawHub packages.

options.title: Full core provenance registry
options.body: Core would own temp artifact classes, registry, cleanup/janitor behavior, and durable routing policy for all first-class OpenClaw-created temp artifacts.

options.title: Keep only narrow bug fixes
options.body: Decline the broad core model and track concrete failures such as backup stale-temp cleanup or volatile state-dir checks as separate bounded issues.

recommendation.title: Core guardrails plus plugin seam
recommendation.body: Core would cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance seam, while workflow-specific classifications such as audit/review staging stay in plugins or ClawHub packages.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a product-boundary and storage-policy decision, and `steipete` has the strongest live maintainer context from the related ClawHub decision and current-main/VISION history.
